heroStrategy.headline: Create High-Quality AI Images & Videos with ByteDance Generative Models
heroStrategy.subheadline: Unlock next-generation generative AI with Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro—advanced foundation models for professional image and video creation.
heroStrategy.designNote: Use an editorial split hero with the copy anchored on the right and a layered visual stack on the left: a large polished output preview, a smaller floating video frame, and thin precision-line annotations. Keep the background warm white/orange with a subtle mesh gradient and soft-shadow cards, using orange brand-accent CTAs only. Make the headline dramatic and oversized, with the product seen as premium creative infrastructure rather than a playful AI demo. Add a dark/light alternating section system below, with at least one dark feature band for Seedance and decorative grid-line orbs in the hero to satisfy the creative direction.

repetitionBreakers: Start with a vivid split hero on the orange brand field, then immediately cool into a clean white trust band.
Use a preview-led how-it-works section instead of a generic step list card grid.
Alternate the product blocks: image section as a visual-first split panel, video section as an accordion-with-visual to change scanning rhythm.
Shift testimonials into a compact, credibility-forward 3-card grid to avoid another large visual block.
Finish with a high-contrast centered pricing-to-action moment so the page closes decisively.
blueprint.pageTitle: Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro | AI Image and Video Generation
blueprint.metaDescription: Explore Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro by ByteDance for professional AI image and video generation, with multimodal control, premium quality, and enterprise-ready creative workflows.

sections.designNote: Content-first split hero. Keep the headline explicit about what this is: professional AI image and video generation. Subheadline should name the audience clearly: creative teams and businesses. The right side should show polished output previews for image and video, not a form. Use one dominant orange Get started button, full-width on mobile. Add a compact benefit strip under the CTA to support warm continuity from the ad.

Logo-first trust band placed immediately after the hero. Use 3-6 recognisable partner/customer logos in a clean static flex-wrap row. Keep it restrained and premium, with small labels only if needed. This should feel like enterprise credibility, not a noisy social-proof block.

Treat this as a two-part product story, not a generic feature dump. First block: Seedream 4.5 in a visual-first split panel with a large output preview and a concise 3-5 point capability list focused on text-to-image, editing, composition, and typography. Second block: Seedance 1.5 Pro flips the balance into a more detailed accordion-with-visual treatment to create contrast and reduce repetition. Keep the image and video capabilities clearly separated, with alternating background cues and strong editorial spacing.

Since no strong customer logo set is provided beyond the proof band, reinforce confidence with a concise metric strip rather than another logo block. Use 3-4 proof metrics such as quality, speed, multimodal control, and professional use fit. Keep it visually light and numeric, with minimal copy.

Use the strongest testimonials only and compress them into a 3-card grid. Prioritize roles that match the audience: creative director, video producer, art director. Keep cards equal-height with short quotes and subtle emphasis on outcomes like turnaround time, synchronized audio-video, and editing precision.

Use compact plan cards with a slight hierarchy, not a dense comparison table. The image model and video model should be separate purchase decisions, each with a clear inclusion list. Keep the visual system minimal and conversion-oriented, with the orange accent reserved for the main action. This section should feel decisive, not salesy.

Final conversion block should be a clean centered card with one primary action: Get started. No secondary CTA. Frame it as the fastest path to see the models in action, matching the warm-traffic rule to favor low-friction evaluation over hard sign-up pressure. Mobile CTA must be full-width.
Low-emphasis utility footer only. Keep it quiet, informational, and narrow. Do not introduce new conversion pressure here.

blueprint.designPersonality: Minimal, premium, and intelligently structured. The page should feel like a curated editorial showcase for enterprise-grade generative AI, with strong logo-led credibility, soft shadows, generous whitespace, and elegant orange brand accents.
blueprint.imageryDirection: Use clean editorial product visuals: abstract model panels, floating output previews, minimal interface shells, and polished mock generations. Favor image-composition scenes, short video frames, and capability cards rather than busy dashboards. Include a prominent logo proof band near the top to make trust the strongest signal.
blueprint.primaryGoal: Drive qualified product evaluation for professional AI image and video generation.
blueprint.narrativeMode: ad-continuity to proof-led product education to decisive conversion

typography.heroFontSizeReason: The headline is long, so a 48px hero size keeps it elegant, readable, and balanced without overcrowding the layout.

colours.colourReason: Using the brand’s locked orange as the primary and accent creates a distinct identity tied directly to Techjockey, while the warm white and soft grey palette keeps the page minimal, clean, and soothing.

referenceMap.heroPattern: Single-screen split hero with brand/logo area, large headline, short supporting copy, and compact benefit list. Strong top-to-bottom hierarchy with one dominant CTA in the lead area and minimal secondary clutter.
referenceMap.sectionRhythm: Hero followed by a lead form block, then stacked product feature sections. Layout favors vertically scrolling, conversion-first sequencing with clear separation between marketing intro and deeper product detail.
referenceMap.cardStyle: Form-centered content card and standard content blocks with solid backgrounds, defined borders, and minimal ornamentation. Visual language is utilitarian rather than decorative, with emphasis on readability and lead capture.
referenceMap.ctaPattern: Primary CTA appears in the hero and conversion sections as a single action-oriented button. Secondary CTAs are either absent or de-emphasized. CTAs are placed near decision points rather than repeated aggressively.
referenceMap.pricingPattern: No visible pricing module in the reference structure. Use a placeholder pricing pattern only if needed: compact plan cards or a comparison table with simple inclusion lists and strong hierarchy.
referenceMap.footerMode: Not visible in the provided reference excerpt; assume a standard informational footer if implemented, with low visual emphasis and utility links only.
referenceMap.mediaPattern: Primarily text-led layout with small brand/logo media in the hero. No strong evidence of large illustration, video, or media panels in the provided excerpt.
referenceMap.productSectionPattern: Sequential feature sections with section labels, headline, paragraph description, and a structured feature list. Each section is self-contained and content-dense, suitable for modular reuse across products.
referenceMap.formPattern: Prominent lead form card directly under the hero, using a focused single-purpose layout with hidden tracking inputs and a compact visible field area. Conversion form is treated as a primary section, not a modal or sidebar.
referenceMap.animationStyle: Static, low-motion presentation with no visible motion system in the provided markup. If animated, keep transitions subtle and functional rather than decorative.
designNotes: Prioritize conversion hierarchy over storytelling flourishes.
Keep copy blocks short and scannable, with a clear headline, short paragraph, then bullets.
Use strong visual separation between hero, form, and product detail sections.
Favor dense information architecture for B2B buyers over decorative layout complexity.
If adapting to this content, preserve the left-to-right split hero and immediate form placement.
The reference suggests a traditional enterprise landing page system rather than a product-gallery or editorial layout.

designStrategy.reasoning: This page is for professionals evaluating advanced AI image and video generation, so the design should feel credible, clear, and conversion-focused rather than playful. Because the user explicitly said logos are the strongest trust signal, the page should prioritize a logo band and brand credibility cues above testimonials or badges. The content is already solution-aware, so the narrative should lead with product capability, then support with feature detail, pricing, and role-specific testimonials. A split hero is the safest choice because it supports strong messaging hierarchy while leaving room for relevant product media without overwhelming the page. The overall style should stay minimal and clean, with balanced spacing and a premium, efficient tone.
